newsitem.title: USA: Ross role said expanded under Albright.
newsitem.headline: Ross role said expanded under Albright.

text.p: Special U.S. Middle East coordinator Dennis Ross is being given broader responsibilities under new Secretary of State Madeleine Albright, U.S. officials said on Thursday.
Ross has spent the last four years focusing almost exclusively on negotiations between Israel and the Palestinians and Israel and Syria.
But he has considerable expertise in Russia and the former Soviet Union and has been told by Albright that his "brief will be expanded" under her tenure, officials told Reuters.

They said all the specifics of Ross' new role did not appear to be worked out but he is expected to accompany Albright on her first overseas trip. Scheduled for February 15 to 25, the trip will cover major capitals in Europe and Asia, not the MIddle East.
One official said even with expanded duties, Ross "still wants to play the leading role on the (Middle East) peace process."

In addition to four years working on the Middle East under former Secretary of State Warren Christopher, Ross was lead strategist and negotiator on the Middle East and the former Soviet Union as a member of the braintrust of Christopher's predecessor, James Baker.
Another official said he understood that Ross "would probably hang on to the Middle East, at least for a while."
An Israeli diplomat said he did not detect any concern in his government that Ross would have an broader role. "We assume that he will still be very involved" in the peace process, he said.
There is some speculation Ross would have a new title, that of State Department counsellor. But officials said he may also be called ambassador-at-large.
